instruction: Add an 'Average' row below the sales data that calculates the average monthly sales across all reps.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent typed 'Total' in A13 (skipping row 12), correctly computed SUM formulas for all 6 months (B13:G13), then attempted to create a chart but produced scatter/points instead of a line chart. Total row values were correct but chart type was wrong.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can type text into cells, use SUM formulas, navigate LibreOffice menus, create charts via Insert menu
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because: (1) placed Total in row 13 instead of row 12, (2) created scatter chart instead of line chart, (3) x-axis showed numbers instead of month names. The SUM computation was correct.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests AVERAGE formula capability, a natural variation of the SUM task the model demonstrated. Same difficulty pattern but different function.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding an Average row with AVERAGE formulas for each month (B-G). Getter scans column A for 'Average' label and reads values from that row. Metric compares each column value against expected averages with 1.0 tolerance to accommodate rounding. Partial credit: each correct column gives 1/6 of total score.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly scans column A for 'Average' label and reads values from columns B-G using openpyxl with data_only=True, which will read computed formula values after LibreOffice saves.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_values') and expected.get('tolerance') directly from the rules dict, which is the correct pattern.
Postconfig properly activates the LibreOffice Calc window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before reading, ensuring formulas are computed and persisted.
Partial credit scoring is well-designed: 1/6 per correct column value across 6 months (B-G), with tolerance of 1.0 to accommodate rounding differences.
Data flow is correct: getter returns {'label_found': True, 'values': {'B': val, ...}} and metric accesses result.get('values', {}).get(col) for comparison.
All 6 monthly average values (B through G) are verified, providing complete coverage of the instruction requirements.
Minor: does not explicitly verify the Average row is positioned 'below' the sales data, but verifying correct label and values is semantically sufficient.
